record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Suppose that f in S. Consider the region D(f ) on the Riemann sphere which is the stereographic projection of the image of the unit disc under f . We can associate with each f in S the spherical area of D(f ). What is min{area of D(f )}, f ∈S and what is the extremal function? (Y. Avci)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f$ holomorphic and univalent on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ that satisfy the normalization $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. For $f\in S$, let $\Omega(f)=f(\mathbb{D})\subset\mathbb{C}$, and let
$$\sigma:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow \mathbb{S}^2\setminus\{N\},\qquad \sigma(w)=\left(\frac{2\operatorname{Re}w}{1+|w|^2},\frac{2\operatorname{Im}w}{1+|w|^2},\frac{|w|^2-1}{|w|^2+1}\right),$$
be the stereographic projection onto the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{S}^2\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ of unit radius (so that the spherical metric on $\mathbb{C}$ pulled back from $\mathbb{S}^2$ has area element $\frac{4\,dA(w)}{(1+|w|^2)^2}$, where $dA$ is the Euclidean area element). Define
$$A(f)=\operatorname{Area}_{\mathbb{S}^2}\bigl(\sigma(\Omega(f))\bigr)=\iint_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{4|f'(z)|^2}{(1+|f(z)|^2)^2}\,dA(z).$$
Determine
$$\inf_{f\in S} A(f),$$
and identify all extremal functions $f\in S$ that attain this infimum (or show that the infimum is not attained).
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up any published resolution attributing the minimum spherical area among the class $S$ to a specific extremal function, nor any survey marking the problem as solved. Its status appears to remain unresolved or at least not widely documented.

status_evidence.title: Stereographic projection - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on stereographic projection; no result on minimum spherical area for class S.
status_evidence.claim: No specific solution to the minimum spherical area problem for univalent functions was located.
